chunks: From him, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Sabbah the Shoemaker, from a man, from Sa'd ibn Tareef the Shoemaker, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'The bull of so-and-so killed my donkey.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Go to Abu Bakr and ask him.' So he went to him and asked him, and he said, 'There is no qawd (blood money/compensation) upon the animals.' So he returned to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and informed him of what Abu Bakr had said.

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Go to Umar and ask him.' So he went to him and asked him, and he said the same as what Abu Bakr had said. So he returned to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and informed him.

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Go to Ali (peace be upon him) and ask him.' So he went to him and asked him, and Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'If the bull was the one who entered upon your donkey in its resting place until it killed it, then its owner is liable (dhamin); and if it was the donkey that entered upon the bull in its resting place, then there is no liability upon its owner.'

He said, 'So he returned to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and informed him. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Praise be to Allah Who made from the People of my Household one who judges by the judgment of the Prophets.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتِي: My Household (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.قَوَد: Blood money or compensation for killing

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on animal liability when one animal kills another?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the jurisprudential superiority of Ali ibn Abi Talib by contrasting his nuanced ruling on animal liability with the simpler opinions of Abu Bakr and Umar. The Prophet’s declaration that Ali’s judgment aligns with that of the Prophets underscores the Shia belief in the continuity of divine legal authority through the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as a key text for establishing the principle that the Imams possess the same authority to derive law as the Prophets themselves.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, fromo Sabbah, from a man, from Sa’ad Bin Tareyf Al Iskaaf, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘A bull of so and so killed my donkey!’ So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to him; ‘Go to Abu Bakr, so ask him’. So he went to him, so he said, ‘There is nothing upon the animals’. So he returned to the Prophet<sup>as</sup> and informed him<sup>saww</sup> of the words of Abu Bakr.

So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Go to Umar, so ask him’. So he asked him, and he said similar to the words of Abu Bakr. So he returned to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and informed him<sup>saww</sup>.

So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Go to Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so ask him<sup>asws</sup>’. So he asked him<sup>asws</sup>, so Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the bull had entered upon your donkey in his sleeping place until it killed it, so its owner is responsible; but if it was that the donkey was the one who entered upon the bull in his sleeping place, so there is no responsibility upon its owner’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So he returned to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and informed him<sup>saww</sup>. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Made from the People<sup>asws</sup> of my<sup>saww</sup> Household one who judges by the judgements of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
